nodes.label: git feature flow
nodes.rationale: The whole workflow exists to control the shape of the graph on main - a short list of merge bubbles, one per feature, plus a few app-level commits, so `git log --graph` on main shows what landed and when without every intermediate commit.

nodes.label: merge asymmetry
nodes.rationale: feature into main is always --no-ff because the merge commit IS the record of the feature; main into feature is a plain merge where fast-forward is preferred, because bubbles inside a feature branch add noise. Rebase and squash are forbidden between these branches unless explicitly asked - both destroy the topology the workflow exists to preserve.

nodes.label: deciding where a change belongs
nodes.rationale: Feature work goes on its feature branch; config, dependencies, tooling, docs and cross-cutting fixes go directly on main; a change touching several features goes as one honest mixed commit on main, because splitting it would create three half-merges and a tangled graph. When the bucket is unclear, ask rather than guess - guessing wrong means rewriting history.

nodes.label: leave merged feature branches alive
nodes.rationale: Branches here are long-lived - the user returns to a feature weeks later, merges main into it again and keeps going. Deleting merged branches is a common git reflex and is wrong in this repo.

nodes.label: never push
nodes.rationale: Pushing is the user's last checkpoint before anything leaves the machine. Local commits and merges are fine; git fetch and other read-only remote commands are the one exception.

nodes.label: stop and report on merge conflicts
nodes.rationale: A conflict during main into feature usually means a real overlap the user needs to see, so never resolve by picking a side automatically and never abort silently.
